title: Sector Watch: Good times for American growth
summary: Despite trade tensions, rising interest rates, and stock market volatility, U.S. stocks are showing continued optimism driven by strong economic growth, lower taxes, and declining unemployment. Fund managers Tony Genua of AGF Investments Inc. and Noah Blackstein of 1832 Asset Management LP are identifying investment opportunities in innovative companies across technology, financial services, and healthcare sectors, focusing on high-growth potential and sustainable expansion. Both managers emphasize active portfolio management and selective stock-picking, with a focus on market leaders and disruptive technologies while managing risk through diversification and profit-taking.

title: What to Expect of Google and Softbank Star Nikesh Arora, Palo Alto Network’s New CEO
summary: Nikesh Arora, former Google and Softbank executive, is set to become the new CEO of Palo Alto Networks on June 6th. Despite lacking cybersecurity experience, Arora is known for his ability to build corporate behemoths and institute financial discipline, which investors hope he will apply to Palo Alto Networks to shore up finances and continue its growth as a platform player in cloud security. The announcement of his appointment has already led to a more than 3% rise in Palo Alto Networks' share price in after-hours trading.

title: The Joy of Cooking—for Kids
summary: America’s Test Kitchen (ATK) is expanding its audience to include children with its new venture, ATK Kids, launching this summer. The program aims to teach kids about cooking and the science behind food through cookbooks, picture books, and online activities, emphasizing that cooking is a practical and creative skill that can foster family connection. Jack Bishop and Molly Birnbaum highlight the importance of learning through mistakes and the social benefits of cooking together.

title: Walmart, Target, Kohl’s see the light at the end of Toys R Us’ tunnel
summary: As Toys R Us exits the U.S. market, major retailers like Walmart, Target, and Kohl's are preparing to significantly expand their toy offerings to capture the vacant market share. Walmart and Target are increasing inventory and store space for toys, while Kohl's and J.C. Penney are adding branded toy products. This shift creates opportunities for these retailers, albeit with potential challenges for toy manufacturers like Hasbro and Mattel who relied on Toys R Us as a key partner.

title: Who has the lowest price on grocery delivery?
summary: Walmart is entering Cincinnati's grocery delivery market, emphasizing transparent pricing and a $9.95 delivery fee without subscriptions or hidden charges, contrasting with rivals like Amazon (Whole Foods) and Kroger. The article compares delivery pricing strategies and fees across Walmart, Amazon, Kroger (Instacart and ClickList), and Meijer, highlighting Kroger's preference for its loyalty card and ClickList for best value. Walmart is training 18,000 personal shoppers nationwide and partnering with DoorDash for deliveries, which will reach Cincinnati customers within four hours.

title: Tech Moves: Remitly hires first chief people officer; Amazon VP of finance leaves for Snap; and more
summary: This article details key personnel changes in the Pacific Northwest tech community, including Remitly hiring its first chief people officer, Ayesha Pacholke. It also reports on Amazon VP of Finance Derek Andersen moving to Snap, and Silicon Valley Bank expanding its Portland team with Jane Ullman. Additionally, Phytelligence's founder Amit Dhingra was promoted to full professor at WSU, highlighting significant career advancements and company developments.

title: What’s Changed: 2018 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Full Life Cycle API Management
summary: Gartner's 2018 Magic Quadrant for Full Life Cycle API Management evaluates 22 providers based on their ability to execute and completeness of vision. The report highlights a shift towards APIs being used for external business channels and partner integrations, with new entrants like Amazon Web Services and Microsoft. Google (Apigee) and CA Technologies led the rankings, while IBM, Software AG, MuleSoft, TIBCO Software, and Red Hat remained leaders.

title: This is how Five Below sets itself apart from Amazon
summary: Five Below distinguishes itself from Amazon by offering unique value through significantly lower prices on similar products, according to a KeyBanc Capital Markets analysis. The analysis suggests that items at Five Below are, on average, over 50% less expensive than at Amazon. This value proposition contributed to Five Below shares rising nearly 22% on the day the article was published.

title: 12 American Companies That Control Tech
summary: This article lists and details the 12 American companies that dominate the tech sector, focusing on their market capitalization, revenue, net income, and number of employees as of May 2018. It highlights the race among top tech companies to reach a $1 trillion valuation and discusses how many of these giants established their market positions by creating innovative, industry-standard products. The analysis also touches on their current strategies and future outlook, particularly regarding emerging technologies like AI, blockchain, and autonomous driving.

title: Amazon is getting ready to crush LaCroix
summary: Amazon and Whole Foods are challenging popular seltzer brand LaCroix by offering steep discounts on their private label 365 Everyday Value sparkling water, particularly targeting Amazon Prime members. This move is part of Amazon's strategy to leverage Whole Foods to compete with major consumer-packaged goods brands. The article also highlights the growing sparkling water market and other competitors like Pepsi's Bubly and Coca-Cola's various brands.

title: Vertical Integration Has Gildan Well-Positioned For Private Label Launch
summary: Gildan Activewear Inc. is leveraging its vertical integration and strong manufacturing capabilities to launch two private label lines later this year, aiming to drive top-line growth and attractive returns. CFO Rhodri Harries highlighted the company's ability to compete on price, manage margins, and expand sales with limited further investment, backed by its robust supply chain and strategic acquisitions. Despite a Q1 2018 dip in income and revenue, Gildan reaffirmed its full-year financial guidance, expressing optimism for balanced organic growth.

title: Lennox iComfort Smart Thermostats Now Compatible With Apple HomeKit
summary: Lennox announced that its iComfort S30 and E30 Smart Thermostats are now compatible with Apple HomeKit, allowing users to control their systems via iOS devices, the Home app, or Siri. This integration enhances security and provides remote access to heating and cooling. The iComfort S30 is also notable as the first communicating thermostat to offer HomeKit compatibility, actively monitoring home conditions and communicating issues to service providers.

title: 30 Notable IT Executive Moves: May 2018
summary: This article details 30 significant IT executive moves that occurred in May 2018, featuring major leadership changes at companies like Xerox, Intel, Office Depot, Amazon, and Cisco. It highlights key personnel shifts, including new CEO appointments, CFO changes, and channel leadership roles across various technology sectors. The piece provides specific names, previous roles, and the new positions these executives have taken, along with explanations for some of the transitions.

title: AT&T’s $85 billion quest for Time Warner: The trial’s greatest hits and misses
summary: This article details the key moments from the AT&T-Time Warner merger trial as U.S. District Judge Richard Leon prepared to issue his decision. It highlights memorable testimonies from CEOs about the merger's potential for driving ad sales and content availability, courtroom observations regarding the judge and witness performances, and the contested economic analysis presented during the proceedings.

title: AT&T Just Got Cleared to Buy Time Warner in a Massive $85 Billion Media Merger
summary: A U.S. District Judge cleared AT&T's $85 billion acquisition of Time Warner, rejecting the Justice Department's request to block the merger. This decision allows AT&T to create a media powerhouse combining its mobile and internet services with Time Warner's content like HBO and CNN. The judge found that the government failed to prove the merger would lead to higher prices for pay-TV subscribers.

title: Time Warner-AT&T deal could pave way for CVS-Aetna acquisition
summary: The Justice Department's approval of the $85.4 billion AT&T-Time Warner merger could have significant implications for the proposed CVS-Aetna acquisition. This development is seen as potentially favorable for CVS, raising expectations for regulators to clear its $69 billion deal with Aetna. The article suggests that less regulatory intervention in large-scale mergers might signal a smoother path for the CVS-Aetna transaction.

title: Global X MSCI Colombia ETF COLO
summary: This article provides current trading information for the Global X MSCI Colombia ETF (COLO), including its price, daily and 52-week ranges, and recent percentage changes. It guides users on how to purchase COLO on the eToro platform and highlights other trending ETFs and related investment guides. The ETF's price has seen a recent increase, and key metrics are detailed for potential investors.

title: Google Invests $550 Million in Chinese Online Shopping Site JD.com
summary: Google is investing $550 million in Chinese online retailer JD.com, deepening its ties with China and intensifying its rivalry with Amazon. This partnership will help both companies expand their retailing presence, with JD.com selling products on Google Shopping to reach consumers in the U.S. and Europe, diversifying beyond China's competitive e-commerce market.

title: Kevin O'Leary's OGIG: Best New Tech ETF?
summary: Kevin O’Leary's O’Shares Global Internet Giants ETF (OGIG), launched on June 5, aims to provide investors with exposure to large global internet and e-commerce companies demonstrating quality and growth potential. The rules-based ETF includes a diverse portfolio of companies, some of which O'Leary notes are experiencing faster growth than well-known giants like Amazon. The article lists OGIG's top 10 holdings as of June 15, 2018.

title: AMBO
summary: Ambow Education Holding Ltd (AMBO) is an education and training services company offering AI-powered phygital solutions through its HybriU platform. The company's recent activities include expanding its global learning network, launching new AI-driven teaching systems and platforms, and forming strategic partnerships to advance hybrid learning and professional training. Ambow has also reported financial results and secured new deals and approvals related to its educational technology.

title: The Supreme Court Will Decide If Apple's App Store Is a Monopoly
summary: The Supreme Court is set to hear Apple Inc. v. Pepper, a case that questions whether Apple's App Store constitutes a monopoly due to its 30 percent commission fee and exclusive distribution model for iOS apps. The outcome could significantly impact antitrust legal precedent and have wide-reaching implications for consumers and other tech companies like Amazon. Central to the case is the 1977 Illinois Brick Doctrine, which Apple argues shields it from consumer lawsuits as developers, not Apple, are the direct sellers of apps.

title: Nestlé and XPO prepare a ‘warehouse of the future’
summary: Nestlé and XPO Logistics are collaborating to build a 638,000-square-foot "warehouse of the future" in Leicestershire, U.K., set to be completed in 2020. This facility will serve as a testbed for advanced logistics technologies, including automation and AI, to enhance Nestlé's supply chain efficiency. The initiative underscores XPO's strategic shift towards becoming a tech-driven 3PL and aims to "future-proof" Nestlé's operations in a competitive market.

title: CVS Health will now deliver prescriptions to your home
summary: CVS Health is launching a nationwide prescription delivery service, along with home deliveries for other drugstore items, at a cost of $4.99 for one or two-day service. This move is part of the second-largest drugstore chain's strategy to enhance customer convenience and compete with online retailers like Amazon. CVS Health, which also plans to expand same-day deliveries and recently announced the acquisition of Aetna Inc., aims to position itself more broadly as a healthcare provider.

title: FedEx Quarterly Earnings Surge on E-Commerce Delivery Boom
summary: FedEx Corp. reported a stronger-than-expected fiscal fourth-quarter profit, driven by the surge in e-commerce package deliveries and increased demand from its freight-hauling business. The company anticipates 2019 earnings between $17 and $17.60 per share, with projected increases in revenue and profit margins. This demonstrates the benefit of heavy investment in automation to meet the growing online shopping demand.

title: Amazon, Berkshire Hathaway and JPMorgan Name C.E.O. for Health Initiative (Published 2018)
summary: Amazon, Berkshire Hathaway, and JPMorgan Chase have appointed Dr. Atul Gawande, a renowned surgeon and writer, as the CEO of their new health care initiative. This move, aiming to overhaul employee health care and address high costs, comes as a surprise given Dr. Gawande's limited experience running a large health care organization. The venture seeks to operate independently and without profit-making incentives, despite skepticism about its detailed plans.

title: Surgeon Atul Gawande selected as CEO of new health care company from Amazon, partners
summary: Dr. Atul Gawande, a prominent physician and writer, has been selected as the chief executive officer of the new health care company launched by Amazon, Berkshire Hathaway, and JPMorgan Chase. The new Boston-based company aims to address health care costs for the founding companies' employees and potentially offer solutions for the broader U.S. health system. Gawande will assume the role on July 9, while maintaining his positions at Harvard and Brigham and Women’s Hospital, and continuing his writing.

title: DroneDeploy and Cloudflare Workers
summary: This article details how DroneDeploy leverages Cloudflare Workers to enhance its drone imagery platform. By pushing authentication to the edge and using Workers to build custom signed URLs, DroneDeploy maintains architectural flexibility across multiple cloud providers and ensures secure delivery of thousands of image tiles to users operating in variable network conditions. The solution allows for advanced edge authentication and prepares for future optimizations using Cloudflare's caching capabilities.

title: Supreme Court tells E-commerce it must collect and pay more taxes
summary: The Supreme Court, in a 5-to-4 decision, overturned a half-century-old doctrine, granting states the power to require out-of-state internet sellers to collect and remit sales taxes. This historic ruling eliminates a competitive advantage for online retailers, especially larger ones like Wayfair, Overstock, and Newegg, by requiring them to collect sales taxes, a task Amazon already undertakes voluntarily. The decision, seen as a constitutional favor for state treasuries and brick-and-mortar stores, was based on the Commerce Clause and rejected the "physical presence" requirement for sales tax collection, although it left room for challenges by smaller internet-only retailers.

title: ETF of the Week: Paul Tudor Jones' Goldman Sachs 'JUST' ETF
summary: This article features the Goldman Sachs JUST U.S. Large Cap Equity ETF (JUST), an exchange-traded fund based on Paul Tudor Jones' nonprofit foundation, Just Capital. The ETF focuses on socially responsible investing by selecting companies engaging in "just business behavior" based on 85 ESG metrics. It aims to provide attractive returns by investing in socially conscious companies, which historically exhibit better financial performance and lower volatility.

title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise CEO Antonio Neri Talks Meg Whitman, Microsoft, and Cloud
summary: HPE CEO Antonio Neri discusses the company's strategic shift to a hybrid IT model and focusing on selling more expensive hardware to conventional businesses, moving away from selling barebone servers to cloud giants. He also talks about the breakup of HP into two companies, the importance of edge computing, and partnerships, particularly with Microsoft Azure, while addressing competition from Dell Technologies.

title: PayPal to Buy Hyperwallet for $400 Million
summary: PayPal Holdings Inc. has agreed to acquire financial-technology company Hyperwallet Systems Inc. for approximately $400 million, a move aimed at enhancing its offerings for managing online and mobile payments for businesses. Hyperwallet helps individuals and small firms receive payments in over 200 countries, and this acquisition is expected to bolster PayPal's growth, especially in the booming online marketplace sector, by connecting both buyers and sellers. The deal follows PayPal's earlier $2.2 billion acquisition of iZettle AB and aligns with its strategy to spend between $1 billion and $3 billion annually on acquisitions.

title: AmEx Turns to Amazon for Credit Card Focused On Small Businesses
summary: American Express is partnering with Amazon.com Inc. to launch a co-branded credit card specifically targeting small businesses. This collaboration marks AmEx's first co-branded agreement with Amazon and Amazon's inaugural small-business card, aiming to expand AmEx's reach within the small and midsize company market. The initiative aligns with AmEx's strategy to become a leading payments and working-capital provider for such enterprises.

title: Clorox, Disney and Pixar: an Incredible(s) Team
summary: Clorox has partnered with Disney and Pixar for a national marketing campaign tied to the release of Incredibles 2, highlighting how Clorox products help set the stage for "incredible moments" in family life. This collaboration builds on a successful prior partnership for the movie Inside Out in 2015. The campaign includes co-branded TV spots, in-store promotions, a sweepstakes, and a Snapchat lens.

title: Amazon Books now open at Bethesda Row
summary: Amazon has opened its second brick-and-mortar bookstore in the Washington D.C. region, located in Bethesda Row. The opening took place on Tuesday, June 26, 2018, marking another physical retail expansion for the e-commerce giant.

title: American Express has a deal with Amazon for card aimed at small businesses
summary: American Express announced a new co-branded Amazon credit card specifically for small businesses, marking Amazon's first small business card and part of a multi-year partnership. This deal provides Amex with a significant platform to attract small business customers and comes shortly after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled in favor of Amex in a lawsuit regarding merchant fees, a decision seen as favorable for companies like Amazon that also charge merchant fees. Amex won this mandate over competitors like J.P. Morgan, leveraging its position as the largest card issuer for U.S. small businesses.

title: 8 Stocks to Buy to Invest in Sports Streaming
summary: This article identifies 8 stocks to invest in sports streaming, a growing market that is challenging traditional TV. It details how major tech and media companies like Amazon, Verizon, Twitter, Facebook, Alphabet, Disney, and Apple are approaching sports streaming, while noting Netflix's decision to avoid this sector. The piece highlights each company's strategy, investments, and partnerships in the live sports content space.

title: Amazon acquires online pharmacy PillPack in move into health care
summary: Amazon announced its acquisition of Boston-based online pharmacy startup PillPack, signaling its entry into the online pharmacy market and the broader healthcare industry. This move is expected to disrupt traditional prescription drug providers like CVS Health and Walgreens Boots Alliance, whose shares fell significantly after the announcement. The acquisition provides Amazon with immediate licensing to sell prescriptions in 49 states, fast-tracking its entry into a highly regulated market, and could lead to increased competition and potentially lower drug prices for consumers.

title: The Chase Finn app goes national after successful test
summary: JP Morgan Chase & Co. announced the national rollout of its Finn app in June 2018. This mobile banking application is specifically designed for Gen Z and was developed with input from millennials during its testing phase.

title: Lovesac soars on $54M IPO
summary: Lovesac debuted on the Nasdaq stock exchange, pricing 3.5 million shares at $16 each, raising $56 million in its initial public offering. Despite being over two decades old and having faced bankruptcy, the company has successfully leveraged its direct-to-consumer model and online sales for furniture, a growing e-commerce sector. Lovesac operates 70 showrooms and specializes in premium bean bag chairs and modular sectionals, with online orders facilitated by its physical presence.

title: The New Amazon Partners Program Can Only Make Amazon Stock Stronger
summary: Amazon is launching the Amazon Delivery Service Partners program to address its last-mile delivery challenges and growing Prime member demand. This program offers entrepreneurs a turnkey solution to start their own delivery businesses, potentially reducing Amazon's reliance on external carriers and helping it gain greater control over delivery costs. This strategic move aims to strengthen Amazon's delivery network and support the continued growth of Amazon Prime and Amazon stock.

title: Amazon Is Serious About the Pharmacy Business After All
summary: Amazon's acquisition of PillPack signals its serious intent to enter the nationwide prescription-drug market, putting the pharmacy industry on alert. This move refutes earlier perceptions that Amazon was only mildly interested in healthcare, as the company had previously let some pharmacy licenses lapse. The deal confirms Amazon's direct entry into mainstream prescription sales, impacting numerous established drugstores.

title: What to know to start an Amazon delivery business
summary: Amazon launched a new program to help individuals in the United States start their own businesses delivering Amazon packages, requiring startup costs from $10,000 and operating 20 to 40 vans with 40 to 100 employees. The program offers support, including discounts on insurance and Amazon-branded vans, and targets those with little to no logistics experience. It provides another delivery option for Amazon without replacing existing package delivery services.
